summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute shortness of breath and chest pain. His symptoms were attributed to acute on chronic systolic heart failure with fluid overload, exacerbated by underlying restrictive lung disease and COPD. He was treated with IV diuretics, leading to improved oxygenation and resolution of congestion. His kidney function, initially impaired due to poor perfusion, improved with diuresis. The chest pain was deemed non-ischemic based on stable troponin and lack of EKG changes. He was discharged home on increased torsemide, with instructions to monitor weight, adhere to a low-sodium diet, continue insulin and cardiac medications, and follow up with counseling for substance use and medication adherence.
